angle_name: Log-weight deformation plus on-orbit signed renewal contraction
mechanism: Replace π−Li by its Stieltjes-Abel transform of ψ−id, keeping the d-sum inside that transform. For X=(y+1)²−1, K=y and 0≤t<y+1, use the exact truncated convolution identity Σ_{d≤y}μ(d)ψ(⌊(X−t)/d⌋)=−Σ_{n≤X−t}μ(n)log n−Σ_{m≤y+1}Λ(m)(M(⌊(X−t)/m⌋)−M(y)), which follows from μ*Λ=−μ·log. Treat the second term as an on-orbit dilation operator acting specifically on M, not as a positive kernel on arbitrary sequences. Decompose the prime logarithmic weight by a smooth dyadic partition, prove a vector-valued window estimate retaining every cross term between the endpoint −μ(n)log n and the Λ(m)M((X−t)/m) renewal term, then recover 1/log p by Stieltjes partial summation. Prime powers are handled recursively: an input |M(u)|≪u^{α+ε} makes their contribution ≪X^{1/4+α/2+ε}, whose exponent map α↦1/4+α/2 contracts to 1/2.
new_leverage: The new ingredient is the exact signed identity μ*Λ=−μ·log combined with the sanctioned canonical backward window. It directly enters the only door left open by obstacle 9: a signed, rather than absolute-value, renewal contraction. It also avoids obstacle 1 because μ(a)Λ(m), the endpoint term, and all dyadic cross terms remain in one quadratic form; no standalone Mertens-energy estimate is recombined by Cauchy–Schwarz.
target_estimate: Signed-renewal square estimate SR(α): uniformly for X=(y+1)²−1 and W=y+1, the Stieltjes square function obtained from A_X(t)=−Σ_{n≤X−t}μ(n)log n−Σ_{m≤y+1}Λ(m)(M(⌊(X−t)/m⌋)−M(y))−Σ_{d≤y}μ(d)⌊(X−t)/d⌋ has window norm (W⁻¹Σ_{t<W}|ℒA_X(t)−Q_X(t)|²)^{1/2}≪ε X^{α+ε}; here ℒ is the explicit 1/log Stieltjes operator and Q_X is the explicit prime-power correction. SR(1/2) gives the requested x^{1+ε} windowed mean square; any SR(α) with α<1 gives rung 1.

obstacle_positions.1_F_closure: Outside the closed class: the proof must estimate the joint μ–Λ–M quadratic form, including signed cross terms, never separate M-energy followed by CS/Hölder.
obstacle_positions.2_fiber_growth: No pair-to-modulus map is used; expansion is organized by the exact convolution variable m and dyadic dilation packets.
obstacle_positions.3_pinned_vs_averaged: The estimate is posed only on the kernel-sanctioned window 0≤t<y+1 behind X=(y+1)²−1, so it cannot discard the canonical pins as exceptional.
obstacle_positions.4_modulus_magnitude: No primorial or full wheel modulus appears; relevant scales are the physical divisors m≤√X.
obstacle_positions.5_parity: This is not a sieve upper bound: μ remains linearly and jointly coupled to Λ, so success would require genuine parity-sensitive cancellation.
obstacle_positions.6_circularity: No pointwise bound for R and no zero enumeration is assumed; the hard input is an explicit Λ–M correlation in physical space. Its difficulty is acknowledged as RH-adjacent.
obstacle_positions.7_finite_range_deception: Computation is only a falsification tool for the proposed contraction and supplies no positive evidence.
obstacle_positions.8_Wigert_floor_jump: No pointwise smoothness is asserted; divisor spikes are absorbed in the exact W≈√X quadratic norm and in the Stieltjes square function.
obstacle_positions.9_renewal_edge: The divergent positive kernel is never bounded absolutely. The proposal is precisely the signed contraction for a μ(a)log a/Λ(m) renewal kernel identified as the sole possible reopening.

kill_test: First verify the finite convolution identity exactly, then test the proposed packet contraction against the zero Mellin mode: for each dyadic P compute on the canonical window the full Gram block between −Σ_{n≤X−t}μ(n)log n and Σ_{P<m≤2P}Λ(m)(M(⌊(X−t)/m⌋)−M(y)). Any formulation claiming an operator norm for arbitrary sequences is killed immediately by f(u)=u^σ, since Σ_{m≤y}Λ(m)m^−σ/log X grows like y^{1−σ}/log X. The route survives only if the actual-M cross term is negative enough; exact data showing a persistent nonnegative normalized cross term near 1 would kill it.
rung1_version: Prove SR(3/4), yielding |S|≪X^{3/4+ε} at canonical pins after the excursion theorem. This is the natural first fixed-power benchmark because the prime-power correction is already X^{3/4+o(1)} by absolute values; improving the signed ψ-renewal part to that scale would give δ=1/4 without first solving the recursive prime-power problem.
plausible_partial: Lean-formalize the truncated identity above, the dyadic Stieltjes transfer from ψ to π, and the recursive prime-power lemma α↦1/4+α/2. Analytically, prove the diagonal and widely separated packet bounds, isolating a single adjacent-packet/zero-frequency correlation as the remaining named obstruction.
weakest_assumption: For some α<1, assume only that the actual Möbius orbit—not every test sequence—satisfies SR(α), with the endpoint/renewal cross terms retained and the same estimate stable under the finitely many smooth cutoffs required by Stieltjes inversion.
